steps.body: Slice a 3D solid with a flat cut and the cut face is a 2D shape — a **cross-section**. A cylinder cut **across** (parallel to its base) shows a **circle**; cut straight **down** through the center, it shows a **rectangle**.

widget.prompt: A cylinder is sliced parallel to its base. What shape is the cross-section?

options.label: A circle
options.feedback: Right — every across-slice of a cylinder matches its circular base.

options.label: A rectangle
options.feedback: The rectangle comes from a DOWNWARD slice — parallel to the base gives a circle.

options.label: A triangle
options.feedback: Nothing about a cylinder is pointed — an across-slice shows a circle.

options.label: An oval
options.feedback: Parallel to the base the cut is a perfect circle — ovals come from tilted cuts.

predict.prompt: Slicing a solid PARALLEL to its base — will the cross-section copy the base's shape?
predict.reveal: A parallel slice meets the solid exactly the way the base does — same outline at every height. Tilt the cut and the story changes.

steps.body: The same solid gives different sections depending on the cut. A rectangular box cut parallel to any face shows that face's rectangle. A square pyramid cut parallel to its base shows a smaller **square**; cut down through its tip, a **triangle**.

explanationVariants: A cut parallel to a square pyramid's base is a smaller square — same shape, shrunk toward the tip.
Base-parallel slices copy the base shape smaller: a square.

widget.prompt: A square pyramid is sliced parallel to its base, halfway up. What is the cross-section?

options.label: A smaller square
options.feedback: Right — base-parallel slices copy the square base, shrinking toward the apex.

options.label: A triangle
options.feedback: Triangles come from cutting DOWN through the tip — parallel to the base gives a smaller square.

options.label: A circle
options.feedback: A pyramid has flat square-based sides — the parallel slice is a smaller square.

options.label: The same-size square
options.feedback: The pyramid narrows toward its tip, so the slice is a SMALLER square.

widget.prompt: A square pyramid is sliced vertically, straight down through its apex (tip). What is the cross-section?

options.label: A triangle
options.feedback: Right — a downward cut through the tip meets the base in a line and the apex in a point: a triangle.

options.label: A square
options.feedback: Squares come from base-PARALLEL cuts — down through the tip gives a triangle.

options.label: A rectangle
options.feedback: The cut narrows to the single apex point at the top — that makes a triangle, not a rectangle.

options.label: A circle
options.feedback: A pyramid has no round parts — the vertical cut is a triangle.

explanationVariants: A cut parallel to a face of a rectangular box shows that face's rectangle.
Box slices parallel to a face are rectangles.

widget.prompt: A rectangular box is sliced parallel to its bottom face. What is the cross-section?

options.label: A rectangle matching the bottom face
options.feedback: Right — every parallel slice of a box copies the face it's parallel to.

options.label: A triangle
options.feedback: Boxes have no slanted parts to make triangles — the slice is the bottom face's rectangle.

options.label: A circle
options.feedback: Boxes are all flat rectangles — the slice is a rectangle.

options.label: A hexagon
options.feedback: A face-parallel cut gives a plain rectangle (hexagons need a very tilted cut).

explanationVariants: Cylinder across → circle; cylinder down → rectangle; pyramid down through tip → triangle.
Each cut copies what it passes through: round base → circle, straight sides → rectangle, tip → triangle.

widget.prompt: Match each slice to its cross-section.

left.label: square pyramid, down through the tip

pairErrors.feedback: The downward cut runs along the cylinder's straight sides — a RECTANGLE; circles come from across-cuts.

widget.missFeedback: Not quite — across a cylinder is a circle, down a cylinder is a rectangle, down through a pyramid's tip is a triangle.
widget.successFeedback: All matched — the cut face copies whatever the blade passes through.

explanationVariants: A cone cut parallel to its base shows a circle (smaller toward the tip); cut down through its tip, a triangle.
Base-parallel: smaller circle. Through the tip: triangle.

widget.prompt: A cone is sliced twice: once parallel to its base, once straight down through its tip. What are the two cross-sections, in that order?

options.label: A smaller circle, then a triangle
options.feedback: Right — base-parallel cuts copy the circular base smaller; the tip-cut narrows to a point, making a triangle.

options.label: A triangle, then a circle
options.feedback: Reversed — PARALLEL to the base gives the circle; DOWN through the tip gives the triangle.

options.label: Two circles
options.feedback: The downward cut meets the tip in a point — that one is a triangle, not a circle.

options.label: A rectangle, then a triangle
options.feedback: A cone's sides slant to a point, so the across-cut is a CIRCLE (rectangles come from cylinders).

hints: Base-parallel cuts always copy the base's shape, shrunk.
A cone's base is a circle; its tip is a single point.
Parallel cut: smaller circle. Tip cut: triangle.

steps.body: A cross-section is the 2D face left by a flat cut — its shape depends on the cut's direction.
takeaways: Base-parallel cuts copy the base (cylinder → circle, pyramid → smaller square).
Vertical cuts through a tip make triangles; through a cylinder, rectangles.
One solid gives many sections — direction decides.
steps.teaser: Next: the course capstone — geometry from every angle.

concept.body: A cross-section is the flat 2D shape where a cut passes through a solid. Base-parallel cuts copy the base (cylinder → circle, square pyramid → smaller square); vertical cuts through a cylinder give rectangles, through a pyramid's tip give triangles.

explanationVariants: A cylinder cut straight down through the center shows a rectangle — the cut runs along the straight sides.
Vertical cylinder cuts give rectangles; across-cuts give circles.

widget.prompt: A cylinder is sliced straight down through its center. What is the cross-section?

options.label: A rectangle
options.feedback: Right — the vertical cut runs down the straight sides: a rectangle.

options.label: A circle
options.feedback: Circles come from ACROSS-cuts — straight down gives a rectangle.

options.label: A triangle
options.feedback: Cylinders have no tip to narrow to — the vertical cut is a rectangle.

options.label: An oval
options.feedback: Ovals come from tilted cuts — straight down is a rectangle.
